title: Design CI compute routing with cache reuse and wall-time measurement
summary: Write a design doc, docs/design/ci-routing.md, for moving compute to CI with per-job local/CI routing, warm caches, no duplicate tests, equal verification strength, fit with parallel jobs, and a before/after wall-time-per-verified-result measure. It is for the owner and design reviewers, follows the planning-first addendum in BRIEF.md (2026-10-16), and is design only.

defaults_applied.how: Design doc with alternatives, reviewed before any build.
Numbers are cited to the request or labeled as estimates.
Measurement of wall time per verified result is the outcome check.
Criteria check routing, caching, and dedupe decisions, not just file existence.
Verifier runs cargo fmt --check and test to confirm nothing else changed.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The 'new planning stage' is the planning-first ordering in the 2026-10-16 BRIEF.md addendum; the doc records planning notes before the design body.
Design only, so the review is requested/recorded, not implemented as code.
CI means GitHub Actions, given .github/ exists.
The 25 min breakdown is the user's figure, not measured by me.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/ci-routing.md states the goal (cut the ~25 min median dispatch-to-outcome, mostly repeated cold cargo builds) and its audience, and cites the producer ~12, verifier ~6, checks ~6 min figures as given by the request (labeled as such, not re-measured).

A routing table decides per job kind (code, tests, docs, design, config, build, study) what runs locally and what in CI, with the rule and reason for each; the verifier's allowed command set is addressed.
Cache strategy is specified: what is cached (cargo registry, target dir, toolchain from rust-toolchain.toml), keys, invalidation on Cargo.lock change, and how cold-start cost is bounded.

Duplicate-test avoidance is specified: one run of cargo test/clippy/fmt per commit SHA, with the verifier reusing the CI result keyed by SHA instead of rerunning, and how a stale or missing result is handled.
A section shows verification is not weakened: every check now run locally still runs somewhere, with a mapping and the failure behavior when CI is unavailable or red (no empty success).
A section explains the fit with parallel job execution (docs/design/parallel-jobs.md): shared caches, concurrency and cost limits, and interaction with the planning-first ordering.
A measurement section defines wall time per verified result, with before and after baselines, data source, sample size, and how a regression is detected.
Alternatives considered are listed with rejection reasons, per the designed default, and the design follows the existing docs/design format (compare parallel-jobs.md).
The doc says it was planned through the planning stage first, and records a review (a reviews/ file or an explicit review request) so the design is reviewed before any build.
Only docs change: no athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflow, or Rust files are modified; cargo fmt --check and cargo test still pass unchanged.

out_of_scope: Changing athena.toml, defaults.toml, or any Rust code
Implementing the planning stage itself or the parallel initiative driver
departures: Slightly lower pass odds: a design doc with many required sections is easy to judge incomplete.
